meta.title: Legal Lexicon — Candidate Queue (Monthly Review)
meta.role: Growing list of terms surfaced in chats, awaiting promotion. Promoted terms are removed here and added to the MASTER.

candidates.gloss: a matter established at the mouths of two or three witnesses
candidates.legalSense: The rule requires independent sources of knowledge, not one testimony repeated. Al-pi is literally 'at the mouth of' — the count is of mouths, not of hearings. Deuteronomy 19:15; 17:6; Numbers 35:30.
candidates.caution: Jezebel satisfied the numeric count with two hired mouths (1 Kings 21:10-13), which proves the number alone never satisfies the rule. The corroboration must be genuine.
candidates.duplicateCheck: Master 7 'Witness' already carries the gloss 'sworn testimony, corroborated.' This may be a refinement of 7 rather than a new entry. Resolve before promotion.

candidates.gloss: the mandatory judicial examination of witnesses
candidates.legalSense: To seek out, inquire, investigate. Deuteronomy 19:18 charges the judges to make diligent inquisition — counting witnesses is not enough; they must be examined separately.
candidates.duplicateCheck: No existing master entry covers the examination itself. Nearest neighbors are 7 Witness and 103 Visit; neither carries the inquiry sense.

candidates.gloss: the offense of carrying a report through the community
candidates.legalSense: From rakal, to trade or peddle. The rakil is the one who moves a report from house to house the way a merchant moves goods. Leviticus 19:16 forbids it in the same breath as standing against a neighbour's blood, placing the talebearer beside the false witness — one corrupts the testimony, the other spreads it.
candidates.duplicateCheck: No master entry covers the carrying of a report. Nearest neighbors are 88 Tongue (evidence that acquits or condemns) and 87 Mouth (where testimony issues); neither carries the peddling sense. Master 134 Diabolos is close in effect but is Greek, and is the party who lodges the false charge rather than the one who circulates it.
candidates.openQuestion: Break flag pending Dutch's ruling. The offense is the working mechanism of the counterfeit court, but it is defined as a prohibition inside Yahuah's own code rather than a usurped office.

candidates.gloss: the pre-trial offense of lifting and circulating an unverified report
candidates.legalSense: Exodus 23:1, 'Thou shalt not raise a false report.' Nasa is to lift and carry; shema is the thing heard; shav is empty, worthless, without substance. The offense is complete before any trial opens — a man picks up something he heard and carries it without establishing it. The verse then joins it to putting the hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness, showing the raised report as the first step toward false testimony.
candidates.duplicateCheck: No master entry covers the pre-trial handling of a report. Joins the existing nasa root family as a fourth legal motion of the same verb: to lift a charge away (16 Forgive), to bear the liability of a charge (122 Nasa Avon), to lift a face in partiality (84 Lift the face), and now to lift an empty report and carry it.

sharesRootProposal.note: One verb, four legal motions: lifting a charge away, bearing a charge, lifting a face, and lifting an empty report.

candidates.openQuestion: Break flag pending Dutch's ruling, same question as Rakil.

candidates.gloss: the firstborn's double share of the estate
candidates.legalSense: Deuteronomy 21:17, 'a double portion of all that he hath.' Literally 'the mouth of two' — the measured share, two parts where every other son takes one. It is a fixed inheritance mechanism, not a blessing: the father is forbidden to reassign it to a favored son.
candidates.duplicateCheck: Master 60 'Birthright' already carries 'the firstborn's legal privilege,' and 54 'Portion' carries 'the assigned legal share.' Pi Shenayim is the measurement itself rather than the status or the share in general. May be a refinement of 60 rather than a new number. Resolve before promotion, same as Ed / Al-pi Shnayim Edim.
candidates.note: If promoted, it makes 2 Kings 2:9 an inheritance claim rather than a request for more power — Elisha asking for the firstborn's share of what Elijah carried.
